name: Gujarati
where: Gujarat — Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara — plus Mumbai and a huge diaspora in the UK, the US and East Africa.
script_note: Devanagari's sister with NO headline bar — the letters hang free. If you read Hindi, you'll decode Gujarati fast; a few letters (ખ ગ જ ટ ણ ફ) look different enough to learn fresh.
difficulty: US Foreign Service Institute Category III (about 1,100 hours to professional proficiency) — grouped with Hindi. The script reads fast for Hindi readers; three genders and the ergative past (મેં … વાંચ્યું) are the real work.

sov.en: I eat rice (word-for-word: I · rice · eat · am — the helper છું is compulsory)

gender_title: Three genders — hiding in the past tense
gender_note: Gujarati has masculine, feminine and neuter like Marathi — but the present tense doesn't care (હું ખાઉં છું for men and women alike). Gender appears in adjectives (સારો/સારી/સારું) and the past tense: ગયો (he went), ગઈ (she went), ગયું (it went).
present_note: Gujarati present tense travels with a helper: the main verb plus છું/છે/છીએ (am/is/are). હું ખાઉં છું is literally 'I eat am' — say both parts or it sounds unfinished.
negation_note: Put નથી (nathī) after the helper: હું જતો નથી (huṁ jato nathī) — I don't go. Past tense works the same: ગયો નથી (gayo nathī) — didn't go.
counting_note: Gujarati counts directly — number + noun, no classifier words:
survival_trio: X ક્યાં છે? (where is X?), ભાડું કેટલું? (how much?), અહીંયા રોકો (stop here). These three handle 80% of travel.
bargaining_script: આ કેટલાનું? → બહુ મોંઘું! → થોડું ઓછું કરો → સારું, લઈશ. Smile through all four steps.

vowels.hint: a as in 'about' — a short neutral uh
ru as in 'rude' — rare, Sanskrit loanwords only
breathy h at word end — rare

consonants.hint: k with a puff of air — looks nothing like Hindi ख, learn it fresh
g as in 'go' — different shape from Hindi ग
g with a puff of air
ng as in 'sing' — rare in daily words
ch with a puff of air
j as in 'jam' — different shape from Hindi ज
j with a puff of air
t with tongue curled back — different shape from Hindi ट
retroflex t with a puff of air
retroflex d with a puff of air
retroflex n — different shape from Hindi ण
dental t with a puff of air (never 'th' as in 'thin')
dental d with a puff of air
p with a puff of air — different shape from Hindi फ
b with a puff of air
same sound as શ in daily speech

greetings.note: જય શ્રી કૃષ્ણ (JSK) among many Hindu Gujaratis
Literally 'I'm in fun' — Gujaratis are always having fun
Long but polite — streets say પ્લીઝ
Said at parting by either side — literally an invitation to come again

pronouns.note: One word for both in daily speech; તેણી (she) is formal writing
Same word as he/she — context decides
પેલી (pelī) for a woman — pointing words
કેમ also means how — and why! Context decides

verbs.note: Word it backwards: મને X ગમે છે (to-me X pleases) — see daily phrases
Deep love only — food and films take ગમે છે

time_words.note: Gujarati splits them: કાલે = tomorrow, ગઈકાલે = yesterday

food_words.note: શાક is also 'curry' — સબ્જી works too

food_phrases.note: A woman says ખાતી નથી (khātī nathī)

colors.note: Adjectives agree with gender: કાળો/કાળી/કાળું (black m/f/n)

daily_phrases.note: જોઈએ છે (want/need) always works this way: મને X જોઈએ છે

culture.en: Nine nights of garba-raas — the whole state dances in circles till late. No experience needed; the circle teaches you.
Kite festival (14 January) — the sky over Ahmedabad disappears under kites. Undhiyu and jalebi on every terrace.
Gujarati New Year, right after Diwali — chopda-pujan for the account books, mithaas for everyone.
White-desert festival in Kutch — moonlight on salt, folk drums, mirror-work tents.
Steamed gram-flour sponge tempered with mustard seeds — breakfast, snack, and proof that steamed beats fried.

classifiers.note: one book — number + noun, no extras
two mangoes — counting form as listed
three people — people count directly too

quiz.explain: નમસ્તે (namaste) is the standard hello — to elders, officials, anyone you respect.

quiz.q: How do you say 'thank you' in Gujarati?
quiz.explain: આભાર (ābhār). માફ કરશો is excuse-me/sorry — don't mix them.

quiz.q: Gujarati script differs from Devanagari mainly in…
quiz.a: having NO headline bar (letters hang free)
opts: having NO headline bar (letters hang free)
quiz.explain: Gujarati dropped Devanagari's headline bar — same family, cleaner look. Hindi readers decode it fast.
તમે (tame) is formal 'you' — safe with every stranger.
પાંચ (pāṁch) = 5. Same root as Hindi पाँच.
વીસ (vīs) = 20 — its own word, like English 'twenty'.
ભાત (bhāt) is cooked rice — uncooked rice is ચોખા.
એક = one, આપો = give (polite). The full polite ordering pattern.
ક્યાં (kyāṁ) = where. X ક્યાં છે? is the whole direction toolkit in three words.
જમણે (jamṇe) = to the right. Left is ડાબે, straight is સીધું.
ભાડું (bhāḍuṁ) = fare, કેટલું = how much. Ask before you sit down.

quiz.q: હું ભાત ખાઉં છું. The word order is…
quiz.a: I · rice · eat · am (verb + helper last)
opts: I · rice · eat · am (verb + helper last)
quiz.explain: Gujarati is subject–object–verb–helper: હું ભાત ખાઉં છું. The helper છું is compulsory.
તમે (tame) is formal and safe everywhere. તું to a stranger is rude.
નથી after the verb negates it: ખાતો નથી = don't eat. A woman says ખાતી નથી.
ગઈ (gaī) — the past tense shows gender: ગયો (he went), ગઈ (she went), ગયું (it went).
મારું (māruṁ) = my, નામ = name. મારું નામ પ્રિયા = my name is Priya.
શીખું છું is present continuous: right now, in progress. Say it to any Gujarati and watch them smile.
પુસ્તક (pustak) = book. એક પુસ્તક = one book.
ઘર (ghar) = house/home. ઘરમાં = at home (માં = in/at).
આ (this) + કેટલાનું (for how much). The market survival sentence.
કાલે (kāle) = tomorrow. Yesterday is ગઈકાલે — Gujarati splits them.
